newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals mixed after firmer open.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals mixed after firmer open.

text.p: New York precious metals futures were mixed after the first hour of trade Tuesday as the complex continued to consolidate after last week's slide.
"The upside was tried early, but there was no follow through and the market struggled as it always does lately on the upside," a floor trader said.
COMEX April gold was off $0.30 at $348.20 an ounce, below an opening high of $349.20.
COMEX March silver was down 2.2 cents at $4.88 after scaling an early peak of $2.92.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $346.05/66 after fixing at $346.30 in London this morning. It closed Monday in New York at $346.40/90.
Concern about European central bank sales continued, traders said. A still-strong dollar undermined demand for gold in other currencies, and Chinese New Year will depress demand temporarily.
But the market became oversold temporarily last week after the break below $350 to a fresh three-year low and needs to consolidate again, analysts said.

The strength of the dollar and decline in the gold price may be making some high-cost gold mines unprofitable, though, analyst said. The price of gold in the South African rand was now at a nine-month low as a result.

"A sharp reversal of the fortunes of the (South African gold mining) industry is now in prospect because of the recent strengthening of the rand," industry consultant Edward Osborn of Edey, Rogers Pty Ltd in South Africa said.

"With capex (capital expenditure) brought into the picture, nearly half of the number of reporting mines (in South Africa), representing 2.45 pct of national production, operated at a loss (in the fourth quarter 1996)," he said.
In the platinum metals group, NYMEX April platinum was up $1.10 at $356.50, with NYMEX March palladium $1.40 higher at $130.00, continuing its rally of the past six weeks.

Negotiations over one-year palladium supply contracts from Russia to Japan, usually held in mid-December, were postponed indefinitely due to a dely in the Russian budget being approved, analysts noted.
The Russian budget was belatedly approved Jan 24.

But long term supply contracts between 13 Japanese companies and Russia expired at the end of December and since then Japanese trade houses have received no platinum from Russia, forcing the spot market price up, traders said.
Russia accounted for about 54 percent of total world annual palladium supply in 1996.
-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641; -email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
